We achieved encouraging scaled-up results on the vibration table using a hybrid defrosting strategy that combines thermal and mechanical defrosting methods. In Q10, we successfully improved our system design and acquired HX for retrofitting both UTS freezers and Copeland reach-in freezers. We initiated the integration and customer discovery activities by laying out the detailed plan and action items associated with each team. In Q11, we simulated the HX's vibration to assess stresses and risks, improved the UTS prototype heat exchanger, and fabricated the Copeland prototype heat exchanger/walk- in freezer. We made progress on customer discovery through a customer discovery workshop, and we projected the BOM and ROI of the technology. In Q12, we improved the freezer prototype with an iterative experimental process, which included several changes and improvements to both the apparatus and procedure. This quarter's effort concluded with a successful experiment that demonstrated significant performance improvement over the baseline. We also made progress on the reach-in freezer prototype at Copeland's Helix Innovation Center by completing shakedown testing and initiating experimentation. In Q13, we continued experimentation in the freezer with iterative process improvement, and we tested multiple variables, including motor speed and frosting length/duration. We improved and iterated the testing procedure and the data processing methods. The Copeland team completed customer discovery interviews, which provided valuable insight and learning. In Q14, we upgraded the control system and instrumentation. A new accelerometer was implemented, which was installed and set up to produce useful data. A continuous vibration test was completed, followed by the reinforcement of the evaporator's mounting flanges. The team completed the first round of noise-reduction efforts, achieving a ~17.5 dB reduction in sound pressure level. In Q15, the reach-in freezer was received after being shipped by the Copeland team, and preparations began to run the system. A second round of noise testing was completed by constructing a duplicate system outside the freezer. This system is lighter and can become a testbed for changing motor size. Boxing the prototype resulted in significant reductions in sound pressure level. Finally, another chest freezer experiment was completed, yielding interesting findings that suggest a hybrid cycle clears the HX coil more effectively than a traditional thermal cycle. In Q16, we completed the preparation and set up the reach-in freezer. The team also starts wrapping up the project by making the prototypes operational.
